num_rectangles: int; required scalar, the number of rectangles N, unit: count; must be a non-negative integer; booleans are not accepted. All rectangle indices are 0-based, running from 0 to N-1; the scalar itself has no index axis. N=0 is allowed, in which case widths, heights and the four arrays in the solution are all empty.
widths: list[float]; required one-dimensional array of length exactly N; its only axis is the rectangle index i, not a spatial coordinate axis. widths[i] is the side length of rectangle i along the horizontal axis in its original orientation; after a 90-degree rotation it becomes the side length along the vertical axis. Each entry must be a strictly positive finite real, represented as a JSON number; integer form is also accepted; booleans or null are not accepted. The unit is length, consistent with heights, container_radius and the solution coordinates; the specific length unit is unspecified. The width and height at the same index belong to the same rectangle; rectangles that cannot fit into the container on their own are allowed in the input.
heights: list[float]; required one-dimensional array of length exactly N; its only axis is the rectangle index i, not a spatial coordinate axis. heights[i] is the side length of rectangle i along the vertical axis in its original orientation; after a 90-degree rotation it becomes the side length along the horizontal axis. Each entry must be a strictly positive finite real, represented as a JSON number; integer form is also accepted; booleans or null are not accepted. The unit is length, consistent with widths, container_radius and the solution coordinates; the specific length unit is unspecified; corresponds entry by entry with widths at the same index.
container_radius: float; required scalar, the fixed radius R of the circular container; must be a strictly positive finite real, represented as a JSON number; integer form is also accepted; booleans or null are not accepted. The unit is length, consistent with the rectangle dimensions and the solution coordinates; the specific length unit is unspecified. The center is fixed at (0,0), with no separate center input; this field has no index axis. Even when N=0, the radius must still be strictly positive.
big_m: float; required scalar, the given constant M in the non-overlap disjunction of the problem statement; unit unspecified, no index axis. Any finite real is allowed, including zero, negative and non-integer values, represented as a JSON number; integer form is also accepted; booleans or null are not accepted. When two rectangles are not both selected, the first branch of the disjunction already holds; when both are selected, the coefficient of M is zero. Therefore M does not change the feasibility meaning of the given constraints and is not required to be non-negative or sufficiently large.
